topic: Military aviation - full throttle on carrier landing (bolter)
question: WHY FULL POWER
WHILE LANDING?
options: To keep the engines from dying
To steer straight on the deck
In case it has to take off again
answer_full: In case it has to take off again
recap: A fighter jet lands on an aircraft carrier, and the pilot pushes the throttle to full power the moment the wheels hit the deck.
explain: Sometimes the tailhook bounces over the cables, or the jet touches down too far along the deck. Pilots call that a bolter.
At idle power, the jet would roll off the end of the deck and drop toward the sea.
At full power it simply flies off, circles around and tries again. If the hook does catch a cable, the pilot pulls the throttle back to idle.
